judged_text: Google deleteEvent fallback is logically dead: in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making calendarId undefined and the delete call fail, leaving orphaned calendar events (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~312)

record.issue_text: Google deleteEvent fallback is logically dead: in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making calendarId undefined and the delete call fail, leaving orphaned calendar events (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~312)

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent`, the fallback branch computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match normal calendars, so `calendarId` becomes `undefined`. That makes the fallback effectively non-functional and can cause deletes to be issued without a valid calendarId (risking failed deletes / orphaned events). Same logical issue appears in `updateEvent`’s `selectedCalendar` fallback.
